name: Jehoiachin (Coniah)
charge: Doing evil as his father Jehoiakim had done; a signet plucked from the Lord's right hand
summary: Eighteen years old and three months on the throne when Nebuchadnezzar came. Jeremiah's word over him is one of the hardest in the book: though Coniah were the signet on my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence; write ye this man childless, for no man of his seed shall prosper sitting upon the throne of David.
offense: Jehoiachin followed his father Jehoiakim in doing evil, and his short reign stood within the judgment already gathering upon Jerusalem (2 Kings 24:8-9). The city possessed a temple and a royal line, but neither could be used as proof that the Lord would indefinitely overlook its bloodshed and covenant-breaking.
judgment: I will give thee into the hand of them that seek thy life, and I will cast thee out, and thy mother that bare thee, into another country, where ye were not born; and there shall ye die. He went out to the king of Babylon with his mother, his servants, his princes and his officers, and was carried away with ten thousand captives and all the craftsmen and smiths. Thirty-seven years later Evil-merodach lifted up his head out of prison and set his throne above the kings that were with him in Babylon: a kindness, still in Babylon.

entries.commentary: In Jehoiakim's days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant three years, then turned and rebelled against him. The Lord sent bands of the Chaldeans, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites against Judah to destroy it according to the word he spake by his prophets. This came upon Judah at the commandment of the Lord to remove them out of his sight for the sins of Manasseh and the innocent blood he shed, which the Lord would not pardon. -

Jehoiakim slept with his fathers and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place. The king of Egypt came no more out of his land, for the king of Babylon had taken all that pertained to Egypt from the river of Egypt to the river Euphrates. Babylon took over as had been prophesied throughout the Bible, in Daniel and in Jeremiah, that Nebuchadnezzar would ransack Jerusalem and the surrounding lands.

Jehoiachin was eighteen years old and reigned three months in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all his fathers had done. The servants of Nebuchadnezzar came up against Jerusalem and besieged it, and the king himself came against the city while it was besieged. Jehoiachin went out to the king of Babylon with his mother, servants, princes, and officers, and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

Nebuchadnezzar carried out all the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, and cut in pieces the vessels of gold Solomon had made, as the Lord had said. He carried away all Jerusalem, all the princes, all the mighty men of valour, ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths, leaving only the poorest of the people of the land. He carried Jehoiachin, the king's mother, wives, and officers to Babylon, along with the men of might and craftsmen and smiths, wanting them to build for him what they had built in their own land, as conquering nations always used Israel's skill and industry. -

The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's father's brother, king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah. Zedekiah was twenty one years old and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all Jehoiakim had done. Through the anger of the Lord it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had cast them out of his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. -

Jeremiah is sent down to the king of Judah's house to command the king to execute judgment and righteousness, deliver the oppressed, and do no violence to the stranger, the fatherless, or the widow. If they obey, kings will keep entering the gates riding in chariots and on horses, but if they will not hear, the Most High swears by Himself that this house shall become a desolation. Many nations will pass by and ask why He did this to so great a city, and the answer is that they forsook His covenant and worshipped other gods.

The people are told not to weep for the dead but to weep sore for him that goes away, Shallum the son of Josiah who reigned in his father's place. Shallum went forth out of his place and shall not return, but shall die in the land where they led him captive and see his native country no more.

Woe is pronounced on Jehoiakim, who builds his house by unrighteousness and his chambers by wrong, using his neighbor's service without wages and painting his wide house with vermilion. His father ate and drank yet did judgment and justice for the poor and needy, and it was well with him, but Jehoiakim's eyes and heart are set only on covetousness, innocent blood, oppression, and violence. Therefore no one will lament him; he shall be buried with the burial of an ass, drawn and cast forth beyond the gates of Jerusalem.

Jerusalem is told to cry from Lebanon and Bashan because all her lovers are destroyed; she would not hear in her prosperity, which has been her manner from her youth. Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, even were he the signet on the Most High's right hand, will be plucked off and given into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar and the Chaldeans whose face he fears, cast out with his mother into a country where they were not born to die. The Most High writes this man childless, for no man of his seed shall prosper sitting upon the throne of David or ruling in Judah anymore; Deacon Marathon and the History of a King class break down this curse of Coniah in fuller detail.

The people of the land take Jehoahaz the son of Josiah and make him king in Jerusalem; he is twenty three years old and reigns three months. The king of Egypt puts him down, condemns the land in a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold, and makes Eliakim his brother king, turning his name to Jehoiakim, and carries Jehoahaz to Egypt.

Jehoiakim is twenty five years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years in Jerusalem, doing evil in the sight of the Lord his God, so Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes up against him and binds him in fetters to carry him to Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar also carries off the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon and puts them in his temple. The Most High set a wicked king over the land because his own people would not do what he said. The power of the earth is in the hand of the Most High, and in due time he sets over it one that is profitable. When Israel will not rule in righteousness, he raises a Nebuchadnezzar; Israel's purpose was never to be wicked and rule at the same time. -

Jehoiachin is eight years old when he begins to reign and reigns three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and he does that which is evil in the sight of the Lord. When the year is expired, Nebuchadnezzar sends and brings him to Babylon with the goodly vessels of the house of the Lord, and makes Zedekiah his brother king over Judah.

Zedekiah is twenty one years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years, and he does evil in the sight of the Lord his God and humbles not himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from the mouth of the Lord. He rebels against Nebuchadnezzar who had made him swear by God, and stiffens his neck and hardens his heart from turning to the Lord God of Israel. The chief priests and people transgress very much after all the abominations of the heathen and pollute the house of the Lord. The Most High sends to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending because he had compassion, but they mock the messengers, despise his words, and misuse his prophets until the wrath of the Lord arises and there is no remedy. -

The Most High brings upon them the king of the Chaldees, who slays their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary and has no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man or him that stooped for age. He gives them all into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, and all the vessels of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king and his princes are brought to Babylon. They burn the house of God, break down the walls of Jerusalem, burn its palaces, and destroy all the goodly vessels, exactly the fierce nation the curses warned of. -

Those who escape the sword are carried away to Babylon, where they are servants to Nebuchadnezzar and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia. This fulfills the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah, that the land would enjoy her sabbaths and lie desolate to fulfill threescore and ten years.

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by Jeremiah might be accomplished, the Most High stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation throughout all his kingdom. Cyrus declares that the Lord God of heaven has given him all the kingdoms of the earth and charged him to build him a house in Jerusalem, and calls any of the Lord's people to go up, showing again that the Most High sets over the earth one that is profitable for his purpose. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign Nebuchadnezzar came with all his host against Jerusalem, pitched against it, and built forts round about it. The city was besieged until the eleventh year of Zedekiah, and the famine prevailed in the city. Because the city was besieged no food, water, or goods could get in, so there was no bread for the people of the land.

The city was broken up and the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were round about the city. The army pursued the king, overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and his army was scattered from him, and they took him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where judgment was given upon him. They slew Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, then put out his eyes, bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon, just as Jeremiah had warned him.

In the fifth month of the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard came to Jerusalem. He burnt the house of the Lord, the king's house, and every great man's house, and the army broke down the walls of Jerusalem round about. He carried away the rest of the people and the fugitives, but left the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen, since the poor could not fend for themselves.

The Chaldeans broke in pieces the pillars of brass, the bases, and the brasen sea that were in the house of the Lord, and carried the brass to Babylon because it was valuable. They took away the pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and vessels of brass, and the firepans and bowls of gold and silver the captain of the guard took away. The two pillars, one sea, and the bases Solomon had made were of brass without weight, the one pillar eighteen cubits high with a brasen chapiter, wreathen work, and pomegranates round about.

The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door. He took an officer over the men of war, five men in the king's presence, the principal scribe of the host, and threescore men of the people found in the city. Nebuzaradan brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and the king smote and slew them there; so Judah was carried away out of their land.

Over the people left in the land Nebuchadnezzar made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor. Gedaliah counselled the captains and their men not to fear to serve the Chaldeans but to dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it would be well with them. But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the royal seed, came with ten men and smote Gedaliah and the Jews and Chaldeans with him, and the people fled to Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans, killing a man who gave wise counsel.

In the thirty seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin, Evilmerodach king of Babylon lifted up his head out of prison and spake kindly to him. He set his throne above the thrones of the other kings in Babylon, changed his prison garments, and let him eat bread continually before him all the days of his life. Jehoiachin was given a continual daily allowance for the rest of his life, a mercy shown at the very end of the account. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The Most High tells Ezekiel to take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel, asking what is thy mother, a lioness that lay down among lions and nourished her whelps among young lions. One of her whelps became a young lion that learned to catch the prey and devoured men, picturing how a particular leader devoured his own people. The nations heard of him, took him in their pit, and brought him with chains unto the land of Egypt, showing that when the leader is judged he is dragged off into captivity.

When the mother saw her hope was lost she took another of her whelps and made him a young lion, and he too learned to catch the prey and devoured men. He knew their desolate places, laid waste their cities, and left the land desolate by the noise of his roaring, so the nations set against him on every side and spread their net over him. The judgment is that the Most High always sends the sword, and the sword is the nations; they came up and set a net and a trap all around Jerusalem so there was no escape. They put him in a ward and chains and brought him to the king of Babylon, so he is no longer roaring like a lion but sits chained in Babylon.

The mother is likened to a vine planted by the waters, fruitful and full of branches, with strong rods for the scepters of them that bear rule, exalted among the thick branches. But she was plucked up in fury and cast down to the ground, meaning cast down from rulership, and the east wind, which is judgment, dried up her fruit. Her strong rods were broken and withered and the fire consumed them, and now she is planted in the wilderness in a dry and thirsty ground with no strong rod left to be a scepter to rule; this is the lamentation.

verses.text: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months. And his mother’s name was Nehushta, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father had done.
At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against Jerusalem, and the city was besieged.
And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against the city, and his servants did besiege it.

And Jehoiachin the king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he, and his mother, and his servants, and his princes, and his officers: and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

And he carried out thence all the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house, and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold which Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the Lord, as the Lord had said.

And he carried away all Jerusalem, and all the princes, and all the mighty men of valour, even ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths: none remained, save the poorest sort of the people of the land.
And he carried away Jehoiachin to Babylon, and the king’s mother, and the king’s wives, and his officers, and the mighty of the land, those carried he into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.
And all the men of might, even seven thousand, and craftsmen and smiths a thousand, all that were strong and apt for war, even them the king of Babylon brought captive to Babylon.
As I live, saith the Lord, though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence;

And I will give thee into the hand of them that seek thy life, and into the hand of them whose face thou fearest, even into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of the Chaldeans.
And I will cast thee out, and thy mother that bare thee, into another country, where ye were not born; and there shall ye die.
But to the land whereunto they desire to return, thither shall they not return.
Is this man Coniah a despised broken idol? is he a vessel wherein is no pleasure? wherefore are they cast out, he and his seed, and are cast into a land which they know not?
O earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the Lord.
Thus saith the Lord, Write ye this man childless, a man that shall not prosper in his days: for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah.
Jehoiachin was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem: and he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.
And when the year was expired, king Nebuchadnezzar sent, and brought him to Babylon, with the goodly vessels of the house of the Lord, and made Zedekiah his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem.

And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the seven and twentieth day of the month, that Evil–merodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison;
And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon;
And changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life.
And his allowance was a continual allowance given him of the king, a daily rate for every day, all the days of his life.
Now when she saw that she had waited, and her hope was lost, then she took another of her whelps, and made him a young lion.
And he went up and down among the lions, he became a young lion, and learned to catch the prey, and devoured men.
And he knew their desolate palaces, and he laid waste their cities; and the land was desolate, and the fulness thereof, by the noise of his roaring.
Then the nations set against him on every side from the provinces, and spread their net over him: he was taken in their pit.
And they put him in ward in chains, and brought him to the king of Babylon: they brought him into holds, that his voice should no more be heard upon the mountains of Israel.
